answers.question: My club mate runs 70 miles a week before a marathon. I'm thinking of doubling to 80 next week to catch up, running twice a day. Would that work?
answers.answer:
No. Going from 40 to 80 miles in one week, with doubles, is the fastest way to reach the start line hurt or flat. Fitness from a hard week takes two to three weeks to show, so a jump now gains little and risks a lot.

You are not behind. Your club mate's 70 miles took years to build. You started this build at about 30 miles a week, and you have already run 20 miles and 6 miles at goal pace.

What moves you toward 3:45 is steady weeks and long runs with marathon-pace miles. Next week goes up to 44 miles, and your biggest weeks will be in the mid to high 40s. Your Monday and Friday rest days are where those sessions turn into fitness, and running twice a day would take them away.

new.analysis:
## How the week went
You ran every planned run at the planned distance and took both rest days. Nothing was skipped or overrun. Holding at 40 miles after the 53-mile week before it was the right call.

Your legs felt heavy early in the week but were fine by Thursday. That tells me your body handled the unplanned 20-miler from Sep 13. It also means you have no stored-up fatigue going into a bigger week.

## The marathon-pace session
Wednesday was the best sign so far in this build. You held about 8:35/mi for 6 miles, right on 3:45 pace, and rated it 7/10 for effort. Your heart rate peaked at 160, well short of your max, so goal pace is not a strain at this point.

## Easy running and heart rate
Your easy runs have settled at about 9:50/mi with a heart rate around 139. That is back to where you were before the August heat and the lost sleep. A steady easy heart rate at the same pace means you are recovering well between sessions.

Only 64% of your running time was in zones 1 and 2 this week. The rest came from the marathon-pace miles and from the long run, where your heart rate sat just above zone 2 for half the time. That is fine for a long run, but a calmer start on Sunday will make the pace miles count for more.

## Why next week looks like this
At five weeks out, the job is to make goal pace feel routine over longer distances. Sunday is the key session. It is also your chance to practise race-day fuelling and shoes. Wednesday's threshold reps raise the pace you can hold comfortably, and that makes 8:35/mi feel easier on race day.

## Volume and what comes next
Next week goes up to 44 miles. That is a modest step from 40 and still below the 53 you handled two weeks ago. With two harder sessions, expect zones 1 and 2 to make up about 60 to 70% of your running time again, which is normal for this kind of week.

Two more building weeks follow, including one more 20-miler. Then the taper starts on Oct 12, three weeks before the race.
